data.hypothesis: Replacing the per-pair square root and division with rsqrtf-based inverse-distance cubing, while algebraically cancelling the target mass, may reduce arithmetic cost. Correctness and performance remain unmeasured for this candidate.
data.notes: Adapted the arithmetic hypothesis from T2; its trial had an infrastructure error and provided no source or measured result. Retained baseline-e1 as the only measured correct source and left src/launch.json unchanged. The candidate must be freshly compiled, checked and timed; no speedup or correctness claim is made.
transformations: Keep one thread per output particle and load its initial state once for reuse.
Use rsqrtf(distSq) and its cube to compute inverse-distance cubed without sqrtf and division.
Cancel the target-mass factor algebraically when accumulating acceleration; retain the self-interaction skip, softening, update order, full-state output, and exact copied mass.
